# Capability map

Part of the [app_registry product brief](../PRODUCT.md).

Milestones that deliver these capabilities are in [`03-roadmap.md`](03-roadmap.md).

Headlines only: each `Cn` is a capability, with the count of Requirements that specify it. Requirement bodies are not rendered here — read them with krill's `get_feature_slice` / `get_requirement_slice` MCP tools, or re-render with detail.

## Artifact recording and publishing

- **C1** — CI can record every artifact it publishes (image or chart), traced back to its build, with no manual step.
- **C2** — An operator can see, for any artifact, whether it is a legal promotion target (promotability), so "what can I promote?" is always answerable.
- **C14** — CI can publish a CLI binary (and, eventually, other non-OCI artifact kinds such as firmware) to durable storage through a registry-brokered, content-addressed upload.
- **C15** — CI workflows and other consumers resolve which artifact kinds exist, and how to acquire or publish them, entirely from the registry — with no hardcoded tool-name or app-name list left anywhere.

## Promotion and history

- **C3** — An operator can promote an artifact to an environment, and that promotion writes back to the gitops repo for ArgoCD to act on.
- **C4** — An operator can see the full SCD2 history of what was promoted to an environment and when, and — on a separate timeline — the SCD2 history of manifest content changes on main, without conflating deploy-state history with source-content history.
- **C7** — An operator can override a chart-managed ArgoCD Application's name per chart, where the default doesn't fit.
- **C11** — A release operator's promotion attempt generates a first-class approval-request scoped to (environment, build); the promotion only executes once that request is approved, and an approver can reject it instead.
- **C12** — (not yet scoped) Ephemeral/per-PR environments.

## Release orchestration

- **C5** — An operator can see per-release build and promotion activity (release-run tracking) rather than only per-artifact state.
- **C13** — A release operator can trigger and drive an entire release (build → publish → record) for manmanv2, leaflab, and app-registry itself from the UI, instead of running gh workflow run by hand.

## Operator surface

- **C6** — An operator has a full read+write operator surface in a live web UI, not just a read-only view of state.
- **C8** — An operator can rely on structured operator-facing logs to diagnose a promotion or recording problem.

## Post-deploy health and rollback

- **C9** — An operator can tell, per promotion, whether the promoted artifact is actually healthy in its environment. (1 FR)
- **C10** — An operator no longer has to manually roll back a bad promotion: the registry automatically promotes back to the prior artifact when post-deploy health checks fail.
